name: Vaginal Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Vaginal Atresia

criteria.description: Complete absence or obliteration of the vaginal canal confirmed by physical examination
Primary amenorrhea in adolescent females with normal secondary sexual characteristics
Imaging evidence (MRI or ultrasound) showing absence or severe hypoplasia of the vaginal lumen
Presence of a normal uterus and ovaries on imaging
No evidence of hematocolpos or hematometra on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent vaginal canal on examination plus imaging confirmation of vaginal atresia in a female with primary amenorrhea
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exclusion of other causes of primary amenorrhea and vaginal obstruction.

laboratory: Normal hormone profile including FSH, LH, estrogen
imaging: MRI showing absence or severe hypoplasia of vaginal canal
Ultrasound demonstrating normal uterus and ovaries
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; may be sporadic or part of syndromic presentations
other: Physical examination revealing absent vaginal introitus
Normal secondary sexual characteristics despite vaginal absence

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of uterus and upper two-thirds of vagina
Presence of vaginal canal with obstructed hymenal membrane
Typically presents with hematocolpos and cyclic pain
Presence of vaginal canal with transverse septum causing obstruction
May have normal menstruation distal to obstruction

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea beyond age 15 with normal secondary sexual characteristics
Cyclic pelvic pain indicating obstructed menstruation
Pelvic mass suggestive of hematometra or hematocolpos
references: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists Practice Bulletin No. 136: Management of Amenorrhea
UpToDate: Congenital anomalies of the vagina and uterus
